description_vi: Nghiên cứu mô hình kết hợp phương tiện xe tải và máy bay không người lái (drone) trong logistics giao nhận hàng hóa chặng cuối (last-mile delivery). related_publications.title: A Stage-based Formulation and Meta-heuristic Algorithm for the Revisit Flying SideKick Traveling Salesman Problem
related_publications.venue: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
related_publications.abstract: In last-mile delivery, coordinating unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs or drones) with traditional ground delivery vehicles offers significant potential for operational efficiency and carbon emissions reduction. This paper investigates the Revisit Flying Sidekick Traveling Salesman Problem (RV-FSTSP), a novel variant of the drone-truck delivery problem that relaxes traditional single-visit restrictions to allow the delivery truck to revisit customer locations and remain stationary while drones launch, deliver, and retrieve multiple payloads. We propose a new stage-based integer programming formulation that overcomes the computational bottlenecks of classical three-index time-indexed models. To solve large-scale instances within practical computing times, we develop a high-performance metaheuristic combining constructive procedures with adaptive neighborhood search. Extensive computational experiments on benchmark instances show that allowing truck revisits reduces total delivery completion time by up to 28.4% compared to classical FSTSP models, establishing a new state of the art for drone-assisted last-mile distribution.

related_publications.title: A 2-Index Stage-Based Formulation and a Construct-Merge-Solve and Adapt Algorithm for the Flying Sidekick Traveling Salesman Problem
related_publications.venue: International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (CITA 2025)
related_publications.abstract: In this work, we present the first 2-index stage-based formulation for the Flying Sidekick Traveling Salesman Problem (FSTSP). Additionally, we propose a Construct-Merge-Solve and Adapt (CMSA) algorithm designed to generate high-quality feasible solutions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm consistently produces good solutions in a fraction of the time required by state-of-the-art mixed-integer linear programming solvers, which often struggle to find even the first feasible solution for large and practical instances.

title_vi: Định vị Cơ sở Cạnh tranh Dưới Mô hình Lựa chọn Khách hàng Cross-Nested Logit

category: Đề tài Nghiên cứu Trọng điểm
description_vi: Đề tài giải quyết bài toán lựa chọn vị trí cơ sở kinh doanh cạnh tranh dưới mô hình hành vi khách hàng Cross-Nested Logit (CNL). Nghiên cứu lần đầu chứng minh bài toán thuộc lớp NP-hard ngay cả với cấu trúc đơn giản, đồng thời biến đổi hàm mục tiêu phi lõm thành bài toán quy hoạch nón lồi số nguyên hỗn hợp (mixed-integer exponential cone convex program) để giải chính xác tối ưu.
description_en: Addresses competitive facility location under customer choice behavior captured by the general Cross-Nested Logit (CNL) model, establishing NP-hardness proofs and transforming the non-concave objective into a mixed-integer exponential cone convex program solvable via outer approximation.
methodology: Outer Approximation Algorithm, Mixed-Integer Exponential Cone Programming, Mathematical Reduction Proofs.

related_publications.title: Competitive Facility Location Under Cross-Nested Logit Customer Choice Model: Hardness and Exact Approaches
related_publications.abstract: We study the competitive facility location problem, in which a firm aims to establish new facilities in a market already occupied by competitors. In this problem, customer behavior is a crucial factor in making optimal location decisions. We explore a general class of customer choice models, known as the cross-nested logit model, which is recognized for its flexibility and generality in predicting people’s choice behavior. To explore the problem, we first demonstrate that it is NP-hard even when there is only one customer class and the cross-nested structure has only two nests. To tackle the challenging facility location problem, we demonstrate that the objective function under a general cross-nested structure is not concave. Interestingly, we show that, by a change of variables, the objective function can be converted to a mixed-integer exponential cone convex program, enabling it to be solved to optimality via an outer approximation algorithm. Extensive experiments show the efficiency of our approach and provide analyses on the benefits of using the cross-nested model in the facility location context.

related_publications.title: Designing effective demand response: A review of behavioral insights, consumer engagement, and operational strategies in energy systems
related_publications.abstract: Demand response (DR) programs help electricity systems balance supply and demand by encouraging consumers to adjust their usage in response to price signals or incentives. While DR can lower peak demand, ease network congestion, and support renewable energy integration, customer participation remains low. Successful design and implementation require a comprehensive understanding of human behavior, motivations, and operational strategies. This review synthesizes insights from behavioral economics, operational research, and energy policy to identify the key determinants of consumer engagement in residential and commercial DR programs. We explore non-financial interventions, such as normative messaging, default settings, and gamification, alongside price-based and incentive-based instruments. Furthermore, we analyze operational challenges including baseline estimation, response fatigue, and network constraints. Finally, we propose an integrated framework for designing human-centric, data-driven DR programs that bridge the gap between technical optimization and consumer adoption in modern smart grid ecosystems.

title_vi: Tối ưu hóa Điều độ Máy tính Song song với Ràng buộc Công việc Xung đột

description_vi: Nghiên cứu tập trung vào bài toán lập lịch các công việc có quan hệ xung đột (không thể thực hiện đồng thời hoặc trên cùng thiết bị) trên các máy song song đồng nhất nhằm tối thiểu hóa thời gian hoàn thành (makespan). related_publications.title: Exact and Metaheuristic Approaches to Minimizing Makespan in Parallel Machine Scheduling with Conflicting Jobs
related_publications.abstract: We address the scheduling conflicting jobs on parallel identical machines problem with makespan minimization, a classical and computationally challenging combinatorial optimization problem arising in modern manufacturing and parallel computing environments. In this problem, certain pairs of jobs cannot be executed simultaneously on the same machine due to shared resource contention or physical constraints represented by a conflict graph. We propose exact Constraint Programming (CP) formulations and two effective metaheuristic algorithms: a multi-neighborhood simulated annealing (MNSA) algorithm and a constraint programming-based large neighborhood search (CP-based LNS). Computational experiments on standard benchmark instances as well as large-scale problem sets demonstrate that our metaheuristics consistently find optimal or near-optimal solutions with superior runtime efficiency compared to general-purpose integer programming solvers.

related_publications.title: On the Hierarchical Directed Capacitated Arc Routing Problem
related_publications.abstract: The Hierarchical Directed Capacitated Arc Routing Problem (HDCARP) is an extension of the Capacitated Arc Routing Problem (CARP), where the arcs of a graph are partitioned into distinct priority classes. Motivated by realistic urban applications such as municipal waste collection and winter road maintenance under strict service priority hierarchies, traversal of these priority classes is governed by precedence constraints or hierarchical objectives. In this paper, we introduce and formalize the HDCARP on directed graphs, develop compact mathematical programming formulations, derive families of valid inequalities, and propose branch-and-cut and advanced metaheuristic search algorithms. Computational experiments on large-scale realistic and benchmark road networks demonstrate the computational efficacy of the proposed formulation and algorithmic frameworks.

related_publications.title: Large Neighborhood and Hybrid Genetic Search for Inventory Routing Problems
related_publications.abstract: The Inventory Routing Problem (IRP) integrates inventory management and vehicle routing decisions to optimize the distribution of goods from a central supplier to multiple customers over a discrete planning horizon. Due to the complex interdependency between inventory holding costs, stock-out risks, and routing costs, the IRP presents significant computational challenges. In this paper, we propose a scalable hybrid metaheuristic that unifies a Large Neighborhood Search (LNS) framework with Hybrid Genetic Search (HGS). A core innovation is a new dynamic programming-based delivery-schedule improvement operator tailored for the IRP, which optimizes the removal and reinsertion of all visits to a customer while accounting for delivery quantities and timing trade-offs. We further extend the approach to a stock-out-allowed setting with penalized unmet demand. Extensive computational experiments on 1,040 benchmark instances demonstrate the superior performance of our algorithm, establishing 365 new best solutions and proving highly effective on newly generated large-scale problem instances.

related_publications.title: MetaPerceptron: A standardized framework for metaheuristic-driven multi-layer perceptron optimization
related_publications.abstract: While traditional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) training primarily relies on gradient descent techniques, these algorithms often suffer from vulnerability to local optima and overfitting in non-convex optimization landscapes. Metaheuristic algorithms (MHAs) have emerged as powerful gradient-free alternatives, yet the lack of a unified, accessible, and standardized software framework has hindered widespread adoption and fair benchmarking. In this paper, we introduce MetaPerceptron, an open-source Python framework designed to standardize the integration, training, and benchmarking of metaheuristic-driven Multi-Layer Perceptrons. Built upon PyTorch, Scikit-Learn, and Mealpy, MetaPerceptron provides a Scikit-learn-compatible API supporting both regression and classification across more than 200 metaheuristic optimizers alongside classical gradient descent algorithms. The library includes built-in hyperparameter tuning, feature selection, pipeline utilities, and over 67 evaluation metrics. Extensive experimental results across benchmark datasets demonstrate the flexibility, robustness, and performance of MetaPerceptron in complex predictive modeling tasks.
